target_customer: Home and field service businesses (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing, pest control and similar), plus franchise groups
problem: Service businesses miss inbound calls and leads outside business hours and have no way to score or coach their call handling. Avoca uses voice AI agents to answer, book and nurture.
business_model: B2B SaaS and usage-based AI agents (Convert, Nurture, Coach) sold to service operators
product_category: Vertical voice AI front office for service businesses

founders.name: Apurva Shrivastava
previous_startups: Described by YC as a second-time founder; earlier venture not named

founders.name: Tyson Chen
education: MIT, computer science (machine learning research on generative AI for drug discovery)

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time voice agents with CRM and dispatch integrations were hard for a small team in 2023, but speech and LLM components were available as APIs.

defensibility.rationale: Voice AI components are widely available and many vendors target the same trades. Integrations with ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro and FieldRoutes and trade-specific call data create modest stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Field service platforms later shipped their own AI receptionist features (Jobber AI Receptionist per a 2026 comparison). Avoca instead lists ServiceTitan and Housecall Pro as integration partners, and no acquisition is reported.

market_need_then: Home service operators lose bookings to missed calls and rely on answering services. Avoca's own materials claim it is on track to book $1B in jobs. At W23 the company started with restaurants before narrowing to the trades, per one profile.

identity.logo: SVG wordmark, design not described by sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, benefit-focused short lines and fragments in plain operator language, for example 'Every moment, handled.'

branding.brand_signature: The AI Front Office for Service Businesses
branding.community_and_virality: Fortune profiled the company at the Series B in April 2026 and a Hacker News thread debated vertical AI for the trades. No merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear tagline and press at the unicorn round, but nothing shows the name itself driving awareness. The name is shared with an unrelated Australian trademark holder and an avocado oil brand in search results.

pivots.to: AI agents for HVAC, plumbing and other service trades
pivots.why: Per one aggregated profile, they built for one customer (Rescue Air) for three months and it brought the first customers. Not confirmed by the company blog.

outcome_analysis: Avoca narrowed to home services voice AI and reached a reported $1B valuation in April 2026 with more than $125M raised across seed, Series A and Series B. The site claims 1,000 plus service leaders as customers and integrations with the main field service platforms. The pivot to a vertical with clear missed-call pain and the voice model tailwind appear to explain the growth. Revenue is not disclosed.
notes: Total raised is stated as more than $125M across seed, Series A and Series B by the company blog; individual round amounts and Series A and seed dates are not disclosed there. The site banner reads '$125M Series B at $1B valuation' while the blog text frames $125M as the total, so no Series B amount is recorded. One aggregator reported a Series B led by General Catalyst in May 2024 and another a total of $162.1M; both conflict with the April 2026 announcement and are ignored. A search snippet says Y Combinator led the seed in 2024, unverified. Founder titles (CEO, CTO) come from press snippets. The Fortune page could not be fetched (rate limit), so the Fortune URL is only cited from search results. Competition list is empty because no sources dated near W23 were found; the competitors seen (Studio98ai, Driive, Smith.ai) came from 2026 pages. YC directory status is Active; the outcome search found no layoffs, lawsuits or acquisition.
